## Does chain of thought need scale?

Wei et al. find that the gain from chain-of-thought prompting is missing in small models. It appears only once a model is large enough, so I want to know how sharp that threshold is.

“chain-of-thought prompting does not positively impact performance for small models, and only yields performance gains when used with models of ∼100B parameters.” [wei2022chainofthought, p. 4](labshelf:wei2022chainofthought#p4:0.1765,0.8565,0.6476,0.0388)

A logistic curve in the model size $N$ (billions of parameters) describes the transition well enough. It has a floor $a$, a ceiling $b$ and a midpoint $N_0$ where the gain switches on:

$$
\mathrm{acc}(N) = a + \frac{b - a}{1 + (N_0 / N)^{k}}
$$ {#eq-emergence}

```{python}
#| label: emergence
#| param: n0 = slider(30, 600, 150, step = 10)
#| param: k = slider(0.5, 4, 2, step = 0.1)
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# GSM8K solve rate (%), Wei et al. 2022, Table 1 (four model families)
size = np.array([20, 137, 175, 540])
standard = np.array([4.1, 6.5, 15.6, 17.9])
cot = np.array([4.4, 14.3, 46.9, 56.9])

a, b = 4.0, 60.0
N = np.logspace(1, 3, 200)
curve = a + (b - a) / (1 + (n0 / N) ** k)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
ax.plot(N, curve, color="#2b6cb0", lw=2.2, label=f"fit: N0 = {n0:g}B, k = {k:g}")
ax.scatter(size, cot, color="#2b6cb0", s=46, zorder=3, label="chain of thought")
ax.scatter(size, standard, color="#8a8a8a", s=46, zorder=3, label="standard prompting")
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_ylim(0, 70)
ax.set_xlabel("model size (billions of parameters)")
ax.set_ylabel("GSM8K solve rate (%)")
ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")
for side in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
fig
```
